nodes.description: Heterozygous LMX1A disease can impair cochlear and vestibular function through pathways that remain incompletely resolved. An ongoing maintenance requirement and subtle developmental defects are plausible and may coexist. Congenital cases and cochlear-aperture stenosis in one 2026 proband prevent a universal postdevelopmental-only model. Lmx1a expression becomes restricted to nonsensory epithelia during ear development, so a mature hair-cell-autonomous transcriptional defect should not be assumed. Clinical imaging and progression alone do not distinguish the alternatives.

nodes.description: Dominant disease alleles reduce functional LMX1A activity through heterogeneous lesions, including impaired DNA binding, truncation and, for p.Phe135LeufsTer3, faster decay of transfected mutant RNA. Functional insufficiency does not mean every missense variant lowers protein abundance. Reporter titration favors haploinsufficiency for the tested alleles but does not exclude every alternative effect in native cochlear cells. The 2026 Actinomycin D assay measures RNA stability in transfected HEI-OC1 cells; the authors interpret this as nonsense-mediated decay, without directly testing the surveillance pathway in patient cochlear tissue. No augmentation treatment is established by these experiments.

nodes.description: At P14, Lmx1a-null mice had reduced excitatory-neuron densities in dorsal/ventral cochlear nuclei, aggravated by loss of one Lmx1b copy; double heterozygotes were normal for those measures. Roof-plate Bmp6 expression and Atoh1-positive progenitors were reduced at embryonic stages. P0/P14 apoptosis staining did not increase, without excluding other ages. Central projection defects could also reflect inner-ear abnormalities; tissue-specific conditional studies were proposed rather than performed.

nodes.description: Several dominant LMX1A variants reduce reporter transactivation. The 2026 HEK293 assay used an INS-promoter luciferase construct and found reduced activity for five dominant variants, whereas recessive p.Ile369Thr retained wild-type-like activity. These assays do not identify native auditory targets. Homeodomain and C-terminal changes can impair protein–DNA interaction; a structural study of WNT1/PITX3 promoter recognition and neuronal cells supplies additional noncochlear evidence. A proposed activity–severity correlation from a small allele comparison is not a validated predictor of individual prognosis, especially given wide intrafamilial variability.

These selected observations do not establish that half of all DFNA7 patients have objectively measured dysfunction.
